## Design

### 2026-10-10 – I started on Starbie!

**5h**

I started on Starbie!

This wasn't exactly my first time with KiCAD (I'd done it with stasis and the blinkyboard, but never finished it). I went a bit faster than that, but still took me about 45 minutes to get the schematics done and another 15 to set up the project. So here's a 1hr progress screenshot:

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 180146](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/a7d2639bc4fce04ccebaa2249503106194c6b2974548760c5f6fc953ae1820c8.png)

Yes, I did misspell the project name somehow   : |

In the second hour I got a boundary and the layout done. The boundary looks simple, but it was actually Plan B. I Initially tried to draw a star, but due to my lack of drawing skills, it didn't look like a star. Or rather, it didn't look like a star as much as I wanted it to. So i scrapped it and went for this chamfered rectangle. Below is the 2nd hour progress screenshot:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/2f9b43da034c11f558c6646d6ef50f7720dd8a2a735895a9bb9067c31e44f1f6.png)

I eventually decided that the chamfered corners didn't look very good (and were probably a cut hazard) so i switched to filleted corners. I also added a GND pour like in the guide. Once I started actually routing my pcb, I realized that my layout was NOT going to work (too many intersections.) so I adopted the layout on the original starbie. I ended my 3rd hour with Errors! Yay! Here are all the errors I got, along withe the updated layout:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/d83dfa61e6bb0d5de6c4fdda5ebc33d98b3812ee48c4e80114ecc55c1b829a19.png)

It would be another hour before I actually fixed everything wrong with my pcb. I had to go in and add vias (I know vias would have fixed that too many intersections problem from earlier and allowed me to keep my old layout, but I didn't feel like doing it all over again.) as well as edit my board config to increase some clearances. Heres the pcb with all the errors fixed!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/be468f5a32b4acb33f15f817ed07a4ba2b74d941735d54562cafb2d3aca09c9e.png)

I finished out the board design with some art, including a Hack club flag (which i used the F.Mask layer so its shiny metal) and I gave it a name. It's waffles. I put its name onto the PCB too, but this time in silkscreen (I wanted both types of art on there so yeah) Here it is in 3D view!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/d950830c4d2d4e0577dd0c11d78cbaa522412d3d9edd477de358a2df73de1af5.png)

### 2026-10-11 – I worked on the firmware for Starbie.

**5.6h**

I worked on the firmware for Starbie.

The first hour, I found this website called wokwi and I used it to rebuild my circuit and play around with the starter code. I did this so that any new features that I implement, I could test them out without the hardware. I also decided create a pokemon style evolution system (pokemon fans , I've never played it and if thats not how it works, I am sorry) where you start out with a blob and there's 3 tiers in 2 brancher, aptly named Blocky and Spiky (Yes, I know, very creative) Here's Spiky's 3rd Evolution:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/28b9c3d7809cf564a704addc3a52e13ee07991f19491559e4977a39b3f6695d6.png)

Anyway, I finished 3 of the sprites in this hour.

I spent the next hour finishing up the other 4 sprites and also converting them and putting them into 7 different arrays into my code. Here they are in array format:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/24721f3b9d9b97431f375e64abe967f03c20b89d370d50446c8baabac83889bf.png)

I spent the next hour  figuring out how to actually use the sprites and then starting to implement it.
Eventually I decided to go fully custom and change it from a tamagotchi  (I never understood the point of them, it seems more like a chore than a game??) to a pokemon style thing but battles were tic-tac-toe games. You move your curor by tilting, and click the 1st button to select.

I had these variables by the end of the 3rd hour:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/7280e9cc0e77605c6e0a0835ff3db60a429d4ac3b28c8a7c93245bd2d369d4c5.png)

By the end of the 4th hour, I had my game logic and ready to go, as well as the bot logic. it uses a minimax algorithm, so I didn't need to create an actual neural network. I hadn't tested it, so I didn't know if it worked.

It took me another hour and 45 minutes to get the last bit of touches in, and I for some reason decided to rewrite the accelorometer code instead of grabbing it from the starter repo. It took me a while, but it works!
